what_this_is: SYNTHETIC locality surface sweeps on one RTX 5090, CUDA 13.3. NOT a model-serving speedup.
caveats: graphics clocks could not be pinned on this box; same-box deltas only
prefetch and combined modes carry ~4-5% run-to-run spread, baseline and persist under 1%
key_findings: persist becomes harmful at 4 concurrent sequences and combined loses 21% at 32; the batch-1 policy does not survive batch N (overview 32.5)
the planner reports no oversubscription until 16 sequences, yet persist is already negative at 4 - the hot-set model counts one layer and ignores the other 47
cliff (decline the window when oversubscribed) loses 16 points less than the shipped proportional heuristic at 32 sequences
a 48 MiB persisting set-aside against 64 MiB of streaming traffic costs two thirds of throughput (overview 32.4)
the pre-touch strategy axis spans 1.6 points inside a 4-5% noise floor: unresolved, not solved
partial (half the bytes touched) matches vec4 (all of them): the walk is bandwidth-bound
kernel-integrated (fused) prefetch is 30-33 points WORSE than the separate stream at every distance, overturning the v0.5 roadmap assumption that fusing reduces overhead
state layout alone is a 2.34x effect (head_interleaved 17.81 ms vs linear 7.60 ms) and changes which locality policy wins: persist is +10.5% on linear and -2.5% on head_interleaved
cliff policy scores +22.8% at 16 sequences where every other policy scores -17.4%: a 40-point swing from declining the window instead of shrinking it
reducing pre-touch traffic hurts at batch 1: uniform +21.7%, alternating +14.6%, sparse +5.9%
QoS depends entirely on the shape of the competing traffic: with distinct per-layer weights persist+qos is the best configuration (+8.4% at 64 MiB), with a re-read buffer the same hint costs 3x
bug found by measurement: the streaming window was not clamped to the device access-policy maximum (128 MiB on an RTX 5090), so any weight buffer above that failed outright

qos_absolute_ms.note: absolute ms; control is (baseline, qos off) at each size. reuse re-reads one buffer every layer; distinct gives each layer its own slice.
